implications.CRITICAL_LOW: Profound hypotension / potential circulatory collapse or shock
implications.LOW: Mild to moderate hypotension; assess volume status and orthostatic symptoms
implications.CRITICAL_HIGH: Hypertensive crisis; immediate assessment for end-organ damage required

implications.CRITICAL_LOW: Severely reduced diastolic perfusion pressure; coronary perfusion risk
implications.LOW: Low diastolic pressure; check for volume depletion or vasodilatory state
implications.HIGH: Elevated diastolic pressure; prolonged vascular strain
implications.CRITICAL_HIGH: Hypertensive urgency/crisis; high risk of acute neurological or cardiac events

implications.CRITICAL_LOW: Severe symptomatic bradycardia; evaluate for AV block or sick sinus syndrome
implications.LOW: Mild sinus bradycardia; correlate with athletic conditioning or beta-blocker use
implications.HIGH: Tachycardia; assess for fever, pain, dehydration, anemia, or arrhythmia
implications.CRITICAL_HIGH: Severe tachyarrhythmia; hemodynamically destabilizing, immediate ECG indicated

implications.CRITICAL_LOW: Impending respiratory arrest or profound central nervous system depression
implications.LOW: Bradypnea; evaluate for sedation or metabolic alkalosis
implications.HIGH: Tachypnea; early sensitive marker of systemic distress, sepsis, or acidosis
implications.CRITICAL_HIGH: Severe tachypnea; impending respiratory muscle fatigue and failure

implications.CRITICAL_LOW: Critical hypoxemia; immediate supplemental oxygenation and airway evaluation indicated
implications.LOW: Mild to moderate hypoxia; further pulmonary assessment warranted

implications.CRITICAL_LOW: Clinical hypothermia; assess environmental exposure or severe sepsis
implications.LOW: Subnormal temperature; recheck technique, evaluate frail/elderly baseline
implications.HIGH: Pyrexia / Fever; indicates inflammatory or infectious process
implications.CRITICAL_HIGH: Hyperpyrexia; risk of febrile encephalopathy and cellular injury

implications.CRITICAL_LOW: Neuroglycopenic hypoglycemia crisis; immediate fast-acting glucose required
implications.LOW: Mild hypoglycemia; risk of cognitive impairment and autonomic response
implications.HIGH: Hyperglycemia consistent with impaired glucose metabolism / diabetes
implications.CRITICAL_HIGH: Severe hyperglycemia; assess for ketoacidosis or hyperosmolar crisis

implications.CRITICAL_LOW: Severe hypoglycemia crisis; urgent physician evaluation indicated
implications.LOW: Hypoglycemia; review oral hypoglycemic or insulin timing
implications.CRITICAL_HIGH: Extreme hyperglycemia; high risk of metabolic decompensation

implications.CRITICAL_LOW: Severe symptomatic anemia; potential red cell transfusion threshold
implications.LOW: Anemia; assess iron, B12, or occult blood loss etiology
implications.CRITICAL_HIGH: Hyperviscosity syndrome risk; urgent hematology review

implications.CRITICAL_LOW: Severe thrombocytopenia; high risk of spontaneous mucosal/CNS hemorrhage
implications.LOW: Thrombocytopenia; evaluate drug-induced, viral, or immune etiology
implications.HIGH: Reactive or essential thrombocytosis; monitor thrombosis risk
implications.CRITICAL_HIGH: Extreme thrombocytosis; paradoxically elevated risk of thrombosis or acquired VWD

implications.CRITICAL_LOW: Severe neutropenia / leukopenia; high vulnerability to opportunistic infection
implications.LOW: Mild leukopenia; assess viral suppressive or marrow etiology
implications.HIGH: Leukocytosis; typical response to acute infection, inflammation, or stress
implications.CRITICAL_HIGH: Leukemoid reaction or hematologic malignancy; urgent smear evaluation

implications.HIGH: Elevated creatinine; potential acute kidney injury or chronic renal compromise
implications.CRITICAL_HIGH: Severe renal impairment; monitor electrolyte balance and fluid overload risk
implications.LOW: Low creatinine; often secondary to low muscle mass or cachexia

implications.HIGH: Hyperbilirubinemia / clinical jaundice; hepatic or biliary obstruction pattern
implications.CRITICAL_HIGH: Severe hepatic dysfunction or massive hemolysis
